added_comparison_views.label: Prostrate sandmat — stipule at a hairy node
added_comparison_views.image_role: Stem/node macro / upper-free and lower-fused stipule architecture
added_comparison_views.caption: Find the pale pointed membrane at the leaf-stalk base, to the right of the node. It is a stipule, rather than one of the many fine curved hairs. This single angle locates the structure; turn a real stem over to compare the free upper-side pair with the fused lower-side pair.
added_comparison_views.creator: Stefan.lefnaer

added_comparison_views.label: Matted sandmat — broad fused stipule scale
added_comparison_views.caption: Find the broad pale membrane wrapping across the node below the pink triangular tip. This fused scale contrasts with the narrower pointed stipules in E. prostrata. The original 2 mm scale bar is retained.
added_comparison_views.creator: Stefan.lefnaer

added_comparison_views.label: Hairy sandmat — node location, stipules still unverified
added_comparison_views.image_role: Node close-up / leaf attachments and narrow pale appendages
added_comparison_views.caption: Find the junction of the leaf stalks with the red stem. Narrow pale appendages are visible at the lower-left node, but this photo does not securely distinguish stipules from hairs. Use it to locate the node; distinct filiform stipules remain a missing diagnostic macro.
added_comparison_views.creator: Chet Burrier

added_comparison_views.label: Matted sandmat — root starts at the node
added_comparison_views.image_role: Stem node macro / adventitious root emerging from node
added_comparison_views.caption: Follow the long tan root upward to where it joins the horizontal stem at the leaf node. This directly illustrates adventitious node rooting. A stem lying on soil alone does not prove rooting, and one unrooted node does not exclude E. serpens.
added_comparison_views.creator: Nathan Taylor

added_comparison_views.label: Prostrate sandmat — transverse seed ridges
added_comparison_views.caption: Look at the repeated raised ridges running across each seed. These contrast directly with the smooth seed surface of E. serpens. Use the original 2 mm scale bar for size; the two photographs are displayed at different magnifications.
added_comparison_views.creator: Stefan.lefnaer

added_comparison_views.label: Matted sandmat — smooth seed surface
added_comparison_views.image_role: Mature seed macro / smooth seed surface
added_comparison_views.caption: Look for the absence of the strong repeated transverse ridges visible on E. prostrata. The original 1 mm scale bar is retained. Displayed image size is not seed size; compare sculpture first and read each scale bar separately.
added_comparison_views.creator: Stefan.lefnaer
